content:
We are excited to announce that the 3rd AI for Math Workshop at ICML 2026 has been officially accepted! This year's theme is "Toward Self-Evolving Scientific Agents", pushing the discussion beyond "formalization and theorem proving" toward AI that can verify, generalize across modalities and disciplines, self-improve, and ultimately serve real scientific discovery.

:calendar: Date: July 10 or 11, 2026 | Seoul, South Korea (co-located with ICML 2026)
:www: Website: https://ai4math2026.github.io/
:memo: Submit a Paper: https://openreview.net/group?id=ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/AI4Math

Topics of Interest Formal theorem proving · Autoformalization · Natural language math reasoning · Scientific problem solving · Multimodal reasoning · Verification & evaluation · Human-AI collaboration

Challenge Tracks

  • Track 1: Semantic alignment evaluation in autoformalization
  • Track 2: TCS proofs in Lean 4
  • Track 3: Visual perception-based physics problems
  • Track 4: End-to-end autoformalization & theorem proving

Key Dates

Event Date
Paper Submission Open April 1, 2026
Challenge Open May 1, 2026
Paper Submission Deadline May 25, 2026 (AOE)
Paper Decision Notification June 15, 2026
Challenge Deadline June 15, 2026
Camera-ready Deadline June 25, 2026
Workshop Date July 10 or 11, 2026

Submission Details

  • Format: 2–8 pages (references & supplementary unlimited), ICML 2026 template
  • Review: Double-blind via OpenReview
  • Archival: Non-archival

Reviewer Application We are also recruiting reviewers for the workshop! If you are interested in serving as a reviewer, please fill out the application form: Reviewer Application Form. Reviewers are expected to have publications at top-tier venues and will be assigned approximately 2–4 papers.

We welcome submissions from both academia and industry. Looking forward to seeing your work!

Just a quick reminder.

Two open calls right now from the 3rd AI for Math Workshop @ ICML 2026.
:document: Paper submissions close in 5 days, on May 25, 2026 (AOE), via OpenReview.

We are non archival, so you can submit ongoing work without burning your future venue. Last year's workshop best paper, The Limit of RLVR (Best Paper at the workshop), went on to win NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper Runner-up at perfect reviewer scores . A nice signal of the kind of work the community here helps surface.

:trophy: 2× Best Paper Award ($1,500 each) :military_medal: 3× Honorable Mention ($1,000 each)

Format: 2 to 8 pages, ICML 2026 template, double blind.

:trophy: Challenge tracks now fully live, open today through June 15, 2026 (AOE).

Four tracks across FormalRx, TCS proving, SeePhys Pro: visual physics reasoning, and End-to-End Autoformalization.

Prizes per track: :first_place: $1,000 :second_place: $600 :third_place: $400

More info on the workshop website.

If you have ongoing work in theorem proving, autoformalization, multimodal reasoning, scientific problem solving, verification, or human-AI collaboration, we'd love to see it. Submissions welcome from both academia and industry. :rocket:
